mainTopic: חצי שיעור: oaths, the word אסור, and the מחלוקת of רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש (Yoma 74a)
overview: The amud opens by finishing a challenge to ריש לקיש. He rules that an oath not to eat takes effect even on a half-measure, following רבי עקיבא. That suggests he holds חצי שיעור is not forbidden at all, not even מדרבנן. The גמרא considers saying that an oath takes effect whenever something is permitted מן התורה. It then tests this against the dice-player, whom only the רבנן disqualify, yet a שבועת העדות does not apply to him. The answer is that testimony is different, because the verse ״אם לא יגיד״ requires someone able to testify. Next the גמרא asks whether the word אסור can describe acts that carry כרת. It answers in two ways: אסור means חצי שיעור, or it means the four lighter עינויים learned from שבתון. Then, with גופא, the גמרא lays out the מחלוקת itself. רבי יוחנן says חצי שיעור is forbidden מן התורה because it can combine. ריש לקיש says the Torah only forbids an act of 'eating'. רבי יוחנן challenges him from ״כל חלב״, and ריש לקיש answers that the פסוק is only an אסמכתא. A supporting proof from the כוי is then pushed back, and the reason continues on the next amud.

steps.title: ריש לקיש's oath ruling suggests a half-measure is fully permitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cites ריש לקיש's own ruling that an oath takes effect on a half-measure, following רבי עקיבא, who holds a person can forbid himself even the smallest amount. This suggests ריש לקיש thinks a half-measure is not forbidden at all, not even מדרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this follows רבי עקיבא, who said: A person can forbid himself from any amount at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a challenge against ריש לקיש. It points to his ruling that an oath not to eat takes effect on a half-measure, which follows רבי עקיבא's view that an oath covers even a tiny amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An oath cannot take effect on something that is already forbidden. Yet ריש לקיש rules that an oath does take effect on a half-measure, and according to רבי עקיבא an oath covers even a crumb. The implication is that he holds a half-measure is completely permitted, not even forbidden מדרבנן, and that clashes with the claim that he agrees it is rabbinically forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the opinion of
The תנא whose view is used here
Forbids himself (through an oath)
Any amount at all, even the smallest

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of a challenge. On the previous amud, the גמרא suggested that ריש לקיש agrees a half-measure is forbidden מדרבנן. Here it objects using his own ruling that an oath takes effect on a half-measure, which suggests the half-measure is not forbidden at all.

phrases.english: And it is according to Rabbi Akiva, who said:
A person can forbid himself from any amount at all!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a challenge from the previous amud to the claim that ריש לקיש agrees חצי שיעור is forbidden מדרבנן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Placing the source in a specific case and attributing it to a specific opinion (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzMaskana: Liability for a half-measure comes from an oath, following רבי עקיבא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that ריש לקיש agrees חצי שיעור is forbidden מדרבנן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An oath cannot take effect on something already forbidden. Since ריש לקיש says an oath does take effect on a half-measure, he must hold it is completely permitted.

steps.title: Proposed logic for the oath, and a source raised against it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states the reasoning: since a half-measure is permitted by Torah law, the oath takes effect. It then begins to challenge this by quoting a משנה about שבועת העדות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: since the half-measure is permitted by the Torah, the oath and its קרבן take effect. But we learned in a משנה: The oath of testimony applies only to people who are fit to testify.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא considers a way to deflect the challenge: maybe the oath takes effect because a half-measure is permitted מן התורה, even if it is forbidden מדרבנן. It then quotes a משנה to block that deflection. This is setup, and the real proof comes in step 6.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The deflection assumes that a rabbinic prohibition does not stop a Torah oath from taking effect, and that only a Torah prohibition would block it. The משנה about שבועת העדות is brought to show a case where a rabbinic rule seems to block a Torah oath. That would restore the challenge against ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you say (introduces a possible reasoning)
Permitted by Torah law
The offering brought for violating an oath
An oath about testimony (swearing that one knows no testimony)
Those who are fit to testify

phrases.english: And if you say:

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּאִית לֵיהּ הֶיתֵּר מִן הַתּוֹרָה,
phrases.english: since it has permission from the Torah,
the oath (and its offering) takes effect,
but didn't we learn: The oath of testimony
applies only to those fit to testify.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: כֵּיוָן דְּאִית לֵיהּ הֶיתֵּר מִן הַתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a possible deflection of the challenge in step 1 and starts to rebut it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that a rabbinic prohibition does not block a Torah oath
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup: a משנה about שבועת העדות will show that a rabbinic disqualification does block the oath.

steps.title: What does 'fit to testify' exclude?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא recalls an earlier discussion that asked whom the phrase 'fit to testify' comes to exclude.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we discussed it: What does this come to exclude?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings up an older discussion about that משנה. It asks what the words 'fit to testify' are adding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Women, relatives, and other disqualified people are already excluded elsewhere, so these words must be excluding someone else. The answer to this question will provide the proof against ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: And we discussed it (recalling an earlier analysis)
To exclude what?

phrases.english: And we discussed it: to exclude what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the wording of the משנה quoted in step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which person the phrase 'fit to testify' excludes.

steps.title: רב פפא: it excludes a king
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the phrase excludes a king, who does not testify in court.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: It comes to exclude a king.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives the first answer: the words exclude a king.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A king is not a disqualified witness. He simply does not come to testify, out of respect for the throne. This answer does not help the challenge; the next answer is the one the גמרא will use.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives the first answer
King

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: to exclude a king.

steps.title: רב אחא בר יעקב: it excludes a dice-player
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב says the phrase excludes a משחק בקוביא, a gambler with dice.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: It comes to exclude one who plays with dice.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives a different answer: the words exclude a dice-player. This answer sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A dice-player is disqualified as a witness only by the רבנן, not by the Torah. So if a שבועת העדות does not apply to him, a rabbinic rule is blocking a Torah oath.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives the second answer
One who gambles with dice (rabbinically disqualified witness)

phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Yaakov said:
to exclude one who plays with dice.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב אָמַר: לְמַעוֹטֵי מְשַׂחֵק בְּקוּבְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 3, differing from רב פפא.

steps.title: The dice-player proves a rabbinic rule can block a Torah oath
steps.stepSummary: The dice-player is fit by Torah law and disqualified only by the רבנן, yet the oath does not take effect on him. So a rabbinic prohibition should block the oath on a half-measure too.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a dice-player is fit by Torah law, and it is the רבנן who disqualified him, and still the oath does not take effect on him!
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא delivers the actual challenge to the idea from step 2.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dice-player is Torah-permitted but rabbinically forbidden, and the Torah oath does not take effect on him. In the same way, if a half-measure were rabbinically forbidden, the oath should not take effect on it either. Since ריש לקיש says the oath does take effect, he must hold that a half-measure is not forbidden even מדרבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: By Torah law
He is fully fit
They disqualified him
Takes effect (said of an oath)

steps.whyThisMatters: This tests a basic question: can a rabbinic rule stop a Torah-level law (here, an oath) from taking effect?

phrases.english: But a dice-player:
by Torah law he is fit,
and it is the Sages who disqualified him,
and yet the oath does not take effect on him!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא מְשַׂחֵק בְּקוּבְיָא מִדְּאוֹרָיְיתָא מִיחְזֵי חֲזֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רב אחא בר יעקב's answer to complete the challenge set up in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 2 that a Torah-permitted item allows the oath to take effect despite a rabbinic prohibition
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: With the dice-player, a rabbinic disqualification prevents a Torah oath. So if חצי שיעור were rabbinically forbidden, the oath could not take effect on it. ריש לקיש's ruling that it does take effect shows he holds it is fully permitted.

steps.title: Testimony is different: the verse requires someone who can testify
steps.stepSummary: Testimony is a special case. The verse ״אם לא יגיד״ makes the oath depend on being able to testify, and a dice-player cannot testify at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because the verse says: "If he does not tell." This person is not someone who can tell at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the dice-player case teaches nothing general. A special verse limits שבועת העדות to people who can actually testify.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The oath fails for the dice-player because of the Torah's own wording: the oath is about someone who could tell and did not. Since the court will not accept him, he is not a 'teller' at all. This is a rule of testimony, not a general rule that rabbinic bans block oaths. So an oath can take effect on a half-measure even though it is forbidden מדרבנן, and ריש לקיש can still agree that it is rabbinically forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there
"If he does not tell" (ויקרא ה:א)
Someone capable of giving testimony

steps.whatToRemember: A rabbinic prohibition does not, in general, block a Torah oath. So according to ריש לקיש an oath can take effect on a חצי שיעור. The dice-player is an exception, because the verse ״אם לא יגיד״ ties שבועת העדות to the ability to testify.

phrases.english: It is different there, because the verse says:
"If he does not tell,"

phrases.aramaic: וְהַאי לָאו בַּר הַגָּדָה הוּא כְּלָל.
phrases.english: and this one is not capable of telling at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6 by showing that the dice-player case is not comparable.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction (שאני): a special verse governs the comparison case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Rabbinic disqualifications block Torah oaths in general, as seen with the dice-player.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only שבועת העדות requires the ability to testify, because of ״אם לא יגיד״. An oath not to eat still takes effect on a half-measure.

steps.title: Does the word 'forbidden' also get used for acts that carry כרת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the assumption that אסור only describes things without כרת. It quotes a ברייתא that uses אסור for all five עינויים, even though eating, drinking and work do carry כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it true that whenever a source means 'punished with כרת' it never says 'forbidden'? But a ברייתא teaches: even though they said 'forbidden' about all five, they said 'punished with כרת' only about eating, drinking and doing work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the idea that the word אסור points to something lighter than כרת. It brings a ברייתא where אסור seems to cover acts that do carry כרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The working assumption was that if a source wanted to say כרת, it would say ענוש כרת and not just אסור. The ברייתא seems to use אסור for all five activities, including the three that carry כרת. So אסור might simply mean 'forbidden' in general, and not specifically something lighter.

keyTerms.meaning: Punished with כרת (being cut off spiritually)
Forbidden
But it was taught in a ברייתא (introduces a contradicting source)
With regard to all of them (all five עינויים)

phrases.english: And anywhere that it teaches 'punished with karet,'
does it not teach 'forbidden'?
phrases.notes: A rhetorical question that challenges the assumption.

phrases.english: But it was taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאָמְרוּ אָסוּר בְּכוּלָּן —
phrases.english: Even though they said 'forbidden' about all of them,
they did not say 'punished with karet'
except about one who eats and drinks
and does work, only.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל הֵיכָא דְּתָנֵי עָנוּשׁ כָּרֵת, לָא תָּנֵי אָסוּר? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading that אסור in the list means something lighter than כרת, such as חצי שיעור.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that אסור is never used for an act that carries כרת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא uses אסור for all five עינויים, including the three that carry כרת, so אסור can describe כרת acts too.

steps.title: The ברייתא's 'forbidden' means a half-measure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the ברייתא: אסור refers to חצי שיעור, a full שיעור gets כרת, and כרת applies only to eating, drinking and work.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: when they said 'forbidden,' they meant only about a half-measure. A full measure is punished with כרת. And even though there is כרת, כרת applies only to one who eats, drinks or does work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by explaining the ברייתא differently. The word אסור in the ברייתא is talking about a half-measure, not a full measure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the ברייתא splits into two separate statements. First, אסור covers only חצי שיעור, while a full שיעור carries כרת. Second, among the five activities, כרת exists only for eating, drinking and work. This means אסור still never describes a כרת-level act, so the assumption survives.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it is saying (rereading a source)
About a half-measure (less than the minimum amount)
A full measure (the minimum amount for punishment)

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
When they said 'forbidden,'
they said it only about a half-measure,
but a full measure is punished with karet.
And even though it is punished with karet,
one is punished with karet only for
eating, drinking and doing work, only.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא by rereading the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא uses אסור even for full-measure acts that carry כרת.
steps.terutzMaskana: In the ברייתא, אסור means חצי שיעור only. The כרת clause is a separate statement limiting כרת to eating, drinking and work.

steps.title: Second answer: 'forbidden' refers to the other activities
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: the word אסור refers to the other עינויים (washing, anointing, shoes, marital relations), which have no כרת. They are learned from the word שבתון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you prefer, say: when it teaches 'forbidden,' it refers to the rest. As רבה and רב יוסף taught in the other books of the school of רב: From where do we know that on יום הכפורים it is forbidden to wash, anoint, wear shoes and have marital relations? The verse says 'שבתון,' meaning rest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different answer. The word אסור applies to the four lighter activities, which are forbidden but carry no כרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here אסור does not have to mean חצי שיעור. It describes the other four activities, which are forbidden but carry no כרת. Their source is the word שבתון, read as 'rest from these acts'. Either way, אסור still describes something without כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say (introduces an alternative answer)
About the rest (the other activities)
The books of the school of רב (the ספרי, a halachic מדרש)
שבתון means resting and refraining

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to keep אסור as 'less than כרת': it means חצי שיעור, or it means the four activities learned from שבתון.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the five activities. Eating, drinking and work carry כרת. Washing, anointing, shoes and marital relations do not. Those four are what שבתון teaches.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
when it teaches 'forbidden,' it is about the rest.
As Rabba and Rav Yosef taught
in the other books of the school of Rav:
From where do we know about Yom Kippur
that it is forbidden to wash and to anoint,
and to wear shoes, and to have marital relations?
The verse says: 'Shabbaton' — meaning rest.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא: כִּי קָתָנֵי אָסוּר — אַשְּׁאָרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, independent answer to the קשיא of step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative answer (אי בעית אימא): reassigning which cases the word refers to
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אסור must refer to חצי שיעור of the כרת acts, or else it describes כרת acts.
steps.terutzMaskana: אסור refers to the four other עינויים, which are learned from שבתון and carry no כרת.

steps.title: The dispute itself: is a half-measure forbidden by the Torah?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the core מחלוקת. רבי יוחנן says חצי שיעור is forbidden מן התורה, and ריש לקיש says it is permitted מן התורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now the matter itself. A half-measure: רבי יוחנן says it is forbidden by the Torah. ריש לקיש says it is permitted by the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: With the word גופא, the גמרא opens a fresh look at a dispute it mentioned earlier. It states the two opinions plainly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier discussion depended on whether חצי שיעור is a Torah prohibition. Now the גמרא sets out that disagreement directly. רבי יוחנן says yes; ריש לקיש says the Torah does not forbid it.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself (returning to examine a statement quoted earlier)
Half-measure, any amount less than the minimum
Forbidden by Torah law
Permitted by Torah law (though possibly forbidden מדרבנן)

steps.confusionAlert: Even ריש לקיש agrees that one may not eat a half-measure. He only says the prohibition is not from the Torah; it is מדרבנן.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a famous מחלוקת. The הלכה follows רבי יוחנן, that חצי שיעור is forbidden מן התורה.

phrases.english: The matter itself. A half-measure:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אָסוּר מִן הַתּוֹרָה,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said: it is forbidden by the Torah;

phrases.aramaic: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: מוּתָּר מִן הַתּוֹרָה.
phrases.english: Reish Lakish said: it is permitted by the Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new section that examines the underlying מחלוקת referred to earlier.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: חצי שיעור is forbidden מן התורה. ריש לקיש: it is permitted מן התורה.

steps.title: The reasons behind each opinion
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן's reason: a half-measure can join with more to make a full measure, so it is already forbidden food. ריש לקיש's reason: the Torah forbids 'eating', and less than the minimum is not 'eating'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said it is forbidden by the Torah: since it is fit to combine, he is eating forbidden food. ריש לקיש said it is permitted by the Torah: the Torah said 'eating,' and this is not eating.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning of each side of the dispute it just stated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן looks at the food itself: a half-measure can combine with another half into a punishable amount, so it is real forbidden food. ריש לקיש looks at the act: the Torah's word is אכילה, and an act of eating needs the minimum amount (a כזית). Below that there is no Torah 'eating' at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Fit to combine (with more to make a full measure)
He is eating forbidden food
Eating, which halachically requires a minimum amount (a כזית)
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר אָסוּר מִן הַתּוֹרָה:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said it is forbidden by the Torah:
since it is fit to combine,
he is eating forbidden food.

phrases.aramaic: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר מוּתָּר מִן הַתּוֹרָה:
phrases.english: Reish Lakish said it is permitted by the Torah:
the Merciful One said 'eating,' and there is none.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר אָסוּר מִן הַתּוֹרָה: כֵּיוָן דַּחֲזִי לְאִיצְטְרוֹפֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the two opinions just stated.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: a half-measure is forbidden food because it can combine. ריש לקיש: the Torah forbids only an act of eating, which requires a full שיעור.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן challenges ריש לקיש from the verse 'כל חלב'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן quotes a ברייתא that uses the פסוק כל חלב to forbid even a כוי and a חצי שיעור. This suggests the half-measure prohibition comes from the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן challenged ריש לקיש: I would only know that whatever carries punishment carries a prohibition. A כוי and a half-measure, since they carry no punishment, I might think carry no prohibition. So the verse says 'all fat'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן attacks ריש לקיש's view with a ברייתא. The ברייתא learns from a פסוק that even a half-measure of חלב is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says that cases with no punishment, like a כוי (a doubtful animal) or a half-measure, might seem to have no prohibition either. The extra word כל in כל חלב teaches that they are forbidden. Since a פסוק is the source, it looks like חצי שיעור is forbidden מן התורה, against ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged him (from a תנאי source)
Punishment
Prohibition / Torah warning
An animal of doubtful status, perhaps domestic and perhaps wild
'All fat': the פסוק that includes even partial cases

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan challenged Reish Lakish:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא כֹּל שֶׁיֶּשְׁנוֹ בְּעוֹנֶשׁ
phrases.english: I would only know that whatever carries punishment
carries a prohibition;
a koy and a half-measure,
since they carry no punishment,
I might think they carry no prohibition;
so the verse says: 'all fat'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks ריש לקיש's opinion from step 11–12 using a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that חצי שיעור is permitted מן התורה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא derives the prohibition of a half-measure from the פסוק כל חלב, which implies a Torah-level prohibition.

steps.title: The prohibition is rabbinic; the verse is only a hint
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answers that the half-measure prohibition is only מדרבנן. The פסוק כל חלב is merely an אסמכתא, a supporting hint.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is forbidden by the רבנן, and the verse is merely a support.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש's side answers the challenge. The ברייתא's prohibition is rabbinic, and the פסוק is only used as a hint.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אסמכתא is a פסוק that the חכמים attach to their own rule as a hint or memory aid. It is not a true Torah source. So the ברייתא does not prove that חצי שיעור is forbidden מן התורה, and ריש לקיש's view stands.

keyTerms.meaning: By rabbinic law
A mere support: a פסוק used as a hint for a rabbinic rule, not as its true source

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן says חצי שיעור is forbidden מן התורה because it can combine. ריש לקיש says it is only מדרבנן, and he reads the פסוק כל חלב as an אסמכתא.

phrases.english: It is rabbinic,
and the verse is merely a support.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends ריש לקיש against רבי יוחנן's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Downgrading the source: the derivation is an אסמכתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's use of the פסוק כל חלב shows a Torah prohibition on חצי שיעור.
steps.terutzMaskana: The prohibition is rabbinic, and the פסוק is only an אסמכתא, so ריש לקיש's view stands.

steps.title: Logical support that the verse is only a hint
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports ריש לקיש. A כוי is a doubtful animal, and the Torah would never need a פסוק to include a doubt, so the ברייתא must be using the פסוק only as an אסמכתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: So too, it makes sense this way. If you think the ברייתא's teaching is a Torah law, there is a problem: a כוי is a doubt. Would a פסוק be needed to include a doubt?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a logical argument that supports ריש לקיש's answer from the last step. The argument is that the ברייתא's use of the פסוק cannot be a real Torah source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We are not sure whether a כוי is a wild animal (חיה) or a domestic animal (בהמה), so it is a ספק. For ה׳ nothing is in doubt, so the Torah has no reason to write a special rule for a doubtful case. Since the ברייתא uses the פסוק to include a כוי, the פסוק must be only an אסמכתא, and the same would then be true for חצי שיעור.

keyTerms.meaning: So too it is logical. This phrase introduces support for the view just stated.
It enters your mind, meaning 'if you were to think'
An animal whose status is uncertain: we do not know if it is a חיה or a בהמה
A doubt, an uncertain case
To include, to bring in an extra case

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the Torah is unsure about the כוי. The doubt belongs only to us. That is exactly the point: the Torah would not write a פסוק just to cover our doubt.

phrases.english: So too, it is reasonable,
phrases.notes: This supports ריש לקיש's claim that the פסוק is an אסמכתא.

phrases.english: for if it should enter your mind that it is Torah law,
a koy is a case of doubt,
phrases.notes: We do not know whether it is a wild or a domestic animal.

phrases.english: would a verse be needed to include a doubt?
phrases.notes: This is a rhetorical question. The expected answer is no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It supports the תירוץ in step 14, which said the פסוק כל חלב is only an אסמכתא.
steps.raayaObject: ריש לקיש's claim that the ברייתא's derivation is only an אסמכתא, so חצי שיעור is forbidden only מדרבנן
steps.raayaSupportSource: The logical principle that the Torah does not write a פסוק to include a case of doubt such as a כוי

steps.title: The support is not conclusive
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the support from step 15. It begins to explain that the חכמים of the ברייתא may have held a view that makes the פסוק a real source after all.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the proof is because of this, it is no proof. They hold that...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the support it just brought. It begins to explain the view of the ברייתא's חכמים, and that explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase לא איריא means the argument does not force the conclusion. The word קסברי opens an alternate explanation of what the חכמים of the ברייתא believed. That explanation will show that the פסוק could be a real Torah source even for a כוי. So the proof for ריש לקיש is weakened, but the reason has not yet been given.

keyTerms.meaning: If it is because of this reason
It is not a proof. The argument does not hold.
They hold, they are of the opinion

steps.confusionAlert: This step stops in the middle of a sentence. The word קסברי introduces the reason, which comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: If it is because of this —
it is no proof,
they hold...
phrases.notes: The Sages of the ברייתא. Their view is explained on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It rejects the supporting logic brought in step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the supporting proof from the כוי being a doubt is rejected. ריש לקיש's position itself is not rejected.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumes the ברייתא's Sages treated the כוי as a mere doubt. They may have held a different view of the כוי, explained on the next amud.
